newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile raises pension fund investment cap - sources.
newsitem.headline: Chile raises pension fund investment cap - sources.

text.p: Chile's Central Bank has decided to raise the overseas investment limit on the country's cash-rich pension to 12 percent of total assets, from nine percent currently, sources at the bank said.
The measure, to be announced shortly, followed a welter of other changes in foreign exchange rules seen likely to stimulate overseas investment by Chilean firms and announced Wednesday.
The bank's governing council decided to raise pension funds' legal overseas investment limit "as part of the measures taken to open up capital flows," said a source at the bank.

Chile's private pension funds are sitting on reserves of over $30 billion, giving Chileans one of the highest personal savings rates outside Asia. But only about $175 million of that, or 0.19 percent, is currently invested in overseas instruments, so the effect of the new rule will be muted in the short-term.

As another measure aimed at encouraging Chileans to invest abroad, the Central Bank last week allowed the country's private banks to start making loans for foreign trade operations between third countries. In other words, a Chilean bank may now lend money for foreign trade operations that don't involve Chile as either exporter or importer.
